title: Rendered parity coverage matrix at the vendored authority checkpoint

authority.kind: vendored Noisemaker runtime pinned by vendor.lock.json

checkpoint.comparisonDescription: Every rendered effect runs twice through independent programs: once on the reference WebGL2Backend and once on the public CablesWebGL2Backend (Cables CGL) adapter, with identical deterministic inputs, audio/MIDI state, and external media texture. RGBA float readbacks of the presented internal texture are compared pixel-for-pixel with a zero mismatched-channel ceiling; the adapter's internal texture must also copy bit-exactly to the stable CGL output texture, and both readbacks must be finite. Per-effect GL resource accounting on both contexts must return to baseline (host resource check).

overlaySettle.behavior: These three effects draw their overlay through async 2D-canvas generation that continues past pipeline initialization (progress uploads on every few strokes; each upload crosses the adapter's guarded shared-CGL state transition, so the drawing needs several seconds on that side). Before capture the harness drains the generation to completion: after the initial quiet period it waits until no overlay source upload has occurred for 1500ms, with a 60000ms cap that fails the case visibly instead of capturing a partially drawn overlay. Both sides therefore compare the same fully drawn overlay, and the zero-mismatch ceiling applies to them on every repeated run like every other rendered effect.

checkpoint.compilerFixtureNote: Compilation itself is not a parity claim: the independent authority comparison is rendered pixels, not graph equality.

sources.catalogPrograms: vendor-cache/effects/manifest.json (210 effect IDs) with programs generated by parity/catalog-inputs.js; overrides in test/browser/harness/pipeline.js SPECIAL_CATALOG_DSL and EXTRA_CASES
sources.representativePrograms: parity/programs.json (11 programs) plus the parameter/behavior EXTRA_CASES

parameterMatrix.catalogSweep: Each of the 210 effects renders its catalog-default program once against the independent reference at the checkpoint size with zero mismatched channels.
parameterMatrix.representativeSuite: 26 source-bound frame comparisons (test/browser/pixel-parity.spec.js) exercise the parameter dimensions below at the same checkpoint and ceiling.

parameters: noise seed, ridges, and displacement parameters (catalog default programs use seed: 1, ridges: true; landscape fixtures use seed: 4, ridges: true; octaveWarp and cubemap fixtures use seeds 1, 4, and 5)
audio waveform/spectrum color, thickness, and gain (audio-waveform, audio-spectrum)
midi grid color, gain, and speed (midi-grid)
landscape filtering: voxel and isosurface define choices (landscape-voxel, landscape-isosurface)
cubemap threshold and per-face basis matrices (six-cubemap-faces, volume-cubemap)

statefulFrames.note: Stateful effects are compared at three frames so accumulated state, not just the first pass, is source-bound.

media.note: A deterministic 32x24 external RGBA8 texture is bound through findExternalTextureIds on both sides with identical pixels.

sizes.checkpoint: 64x48 for every catalog and representative case
sizes.beyondCheckpoint: cubemap cases concatenate six face captures; native-host canvas and manual resize run in the standalone smoke (npm run test:standalone)

dimensions.hostResourceChecks: Every catalog sweep iteration snapshots GL object counts (buffers, framebuffers, programs, queries, renderbuffers, samplers, shaders, textures, transform feedbacks, vertex arrays) on both the adapter and reference contexts before and after the effect; any delta fails the sweep as a visible resource-leak failure.

visibility.skips: Every catalog effect must render and compare; any unrendered effect fails the suite.
visibility.refusalsAndTimeouts: Thrown errors from compile, initialize, render, and disposal become failure records with case context (error.task9 diagnostics); context loss breaks the sweep with an explicit failure.
visibility.failures: Comparison failures carry mismatchedChannels, max/mean channel error, and the first divergent pixels.

outOfScope.nativeEditorHost: The native Cables Standalone editor lifecycle runs in the standalone smoke (npm run test:standalone), in the export-kit workflow's weekly and manual runs on Windows x64, Intel macOS, and Linux x64 for Standalone 0.11.0 and 0.11.3.
